  \caption{\textbf{Nine arms on identical folds.} All arms are fitted and scored on the SAME 21 leave-one-combination-out folds of one synthetic benchmark instance ($d=6$, $k=7$, ground-truth interaction rank 2), each fold repeated over 3 seeds, under one shared protocol (800 optimisation steps, batch 128, lr 0.003, 16 integration steps, Adam) and one shared coupling (entropic unbalanced Sinkhorn, $\varepsilon=0.05$, 25 iterations). nED is normalised energy distance, ED(pred, post)/ED(pre, post), so 1.0 is the no-change predictor; the absolute distance and the denominator are given alongside because the ratio hides the scale. Lower is better. \textbf{Grp} is a compact letter display over adjacent paired tests: arms sharing a letter were NOT statistically separated and must not be read as ranked. $^{\ddagger}$ marks arms whose 95\% CI crosses the no-change line. $^{\dagger}$ DeepSetsEndpoint is trained on the paired displacement rather than the shared coupling: it has no integration step, so it would apply the coupling's barycentric projection directly as a map (measured 2.14$\times$ displacement inflation, scoring worse than no change on its own training conditions). The exception is documented rather than hidden. $^{\S}$ The two IHC-FM rows are the SAME architecture with the same parameter allocation, the same initialisation and the same three-stage schedule; the ablation disables the interaction pathway only. Both therefore allocate 16,646 parameters, but the ablation trains only the 10,554 outside the interaction branch (shown in parentheses), while the full model trains all 16,646. \textbf{Power.} UNDERPOWERED FOR A HEADLINE CLAIM. The paired CI excludes zero, but the margin over FactoredAdditiveCFM is +0.135 normalised ED, below the 0.25 threshold the power analysis requires. Report as a small, precisely bounded difference, NOT as a win. \textbf{The interaction hierarchy does not pay for itself on this benchmark.} The within-model ablation is the better-powered comparison, because both arms share fold, seed, initialisation and schedule so fold difficulty and seed luck cancel: the paired difference is +0.015 nED, 95\% CI [-0.024, +0.051], which includes zero (7/21 folds favour the full model, sign test $p=0.189$). The full model is nominally 0.015 nED WORSE, and the effect is null rather than adverse. This null is not a floor effect: the achievable floor on these populations (true field integrated on the same pre cells) is 0.018 nED and removing the true interaction term from that oracle costs 0.292 nED, so there IS interaction signal to capture and roughly 0.41 of the additive velocity magnitude is interaction. Both IHC-FM arms sit at 0.64, still above the interaction-free oracle at 0.31, so the models have not yet reached the additive ceiling and the interaction branch has no headroom to demonstrate value here. We report this as an open negative rather than adjusting the architecture. Case-study columns are pooled normalised ED read back from the organoid LOCO screen and the chronological purged finance split; only three arms were run on real data, and the remaining cells are marked \texttt{--} (not evaluated) rather than back-filled. Parameter counts are matched to IHC-FM's allocation (16,646) by solving each neural baseline's width. $^{c}$ marks a closed-form arm with no trainable parameters: the figure given is its fitted array state (LinearResponse solves a $(1+2k+d)\times d$ ridge coefficient matrix; MatchingMean and PerturbedMean fit a mean displacement vector), and \texttt{--} means the arm fits nothing at all.}
